summary.headline: Akums Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31.9% YoY to INR1,342 crores and EBITDA more than doubled to INR195 crores, driven by CDMO volume growth above 20%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR1,342 crores (+31.9% YoY, +15.1% QoQ) and EBITDA INR195 crores (+106% YoY, +11.5% QoQ), with EBITDA margin of 14.5% versus 9.3% a year ago and 15% in Q1 FY27. CDMO carried the quarter, with revenue of INR1,115 crores (+38.6% YoY) and management citing more than 20% volume growth. PAT rose 168.3% YoY to INR115 crores. Management said the Zambia supply ($25 million) has purchase orders in hand but revenue will now book in Q1 FY28, and the European contract revenue depends on dossier approval, which could take 1-2 quarters.

segments.name: CDMO
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,115 crores (+38.6% YoY, +15.6% QoQ) on volume growth above 20%; EBITDA INR168 crores, nearly doubling YoY but up only 2.9% QoQ. Management cites about 60 days of order-cycle visibility.

segments.name: Domestic branded formulations (Akumentis)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR132 crores (+8.2% YoY, +14.4% QoQ); EBITDA INR24 crores, down 8.9% YoY (INR26 crores) but up 103% QoQ from INR12 crores. Management attributes the YoY EBITDA dip to adding about 200 field force members and an MR base rising from 1,400 to 1,600.

segments.name: International branded formulations
segments.commentary: Revenue INR44 crores (+95.2% YoY, +26.7% QoQ); EBITDA INR9.9 crores (+80.5% YoY, +43.8% QoQ). Current markets are Africa and Southeast Asia, with Latin America, Middle East and Europe targeted.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: Revenue INR29 crores (-35.3% YoY, -9.1% QoQ); EBITDA loss INR5.7 crores vs INR14 crores loss in Q2 FY26 and INR3.9 crores loss in Q1 FY27. Management targets EBITDA breakeven within 3-4 quarters and expects FY loss below FY26.

segments.name: Trade generics
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23 crores (-5.4% YoY, +10.1% QoQ); EBITDA INR1.2 crores, positive for the third straight quarter. Management is keeping a lean, profitable pocket rather than scaling the segment.

guidance_outlook: Zambia: $25 million order (first of two $25 million rounds) fully intact; dispatch in Q4 FY27, with revenue booked in Q1 FY28 after 100-120 days of transit. No Zambia revenue expected in FY27.
Europe: dossier filed; approval could take 1-2 quarters; supplies to start in FY28. Management expects to give a clearer timeline in about one quarter.

Baddi Phase 1 (oral solids, over 6 billion units/year) to be fully operational by Q1 FY28; total Baddi capacity planned at about 12 billion tablets; management expects Baddi to deliver 10-15% of CDMO revenue in three years.
Zambia JV plant expected to be operational in 2029.
Domestic branded formulations: aims to grow in line with IPM (8-10%) by FY28 with improving PCPM and profitability.
Management gives no specific business-level revenue guidance.
API prices expected to rise slightly over the next 2-3 months, with uncertainty beyond that.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 capex about INR210 crores, including about INR43 crores at Baddi; historical annual capex is about INR300 crores. Maintenance capex estimated at about 5% of INR2,400 crores gross block (about INR100 crores).
Baddi Phase 1 (oral solids, 6 billion tablets/year) to be operational in 3-4 months; existing capacity about 50-51 billion units/year. Management says oral solids capex is typically 3x asset turn.
Oriflame: two manufacturing plants acquired for about INR56 crores, integrated in Q2; management expects revenue to rise about 3x at peak as the company enters colour cosmetics.
Funding: a mix of debt (if cheaper) and liquidation of investments; no firm split given.
demand_pricing: CDMO volume growth above 20% YoY and above 20% QoQ across the last four quarters, spanning existing and new, prescription, private-label and regional customers.
Utilisation above 50%; company says demand outlook for CDMO remains strong.
API prices up 2-3% QoQ and 5-7% over the year as a basket, driven by KSM, husk and solvent costs.
Akumentis gross margin of 74-75%; new product launches contributed about half of growth; about 30 DCGI approvals per year (2-3 per month).
Over 90% of revenue (about 90-92%) from India; 2 CEPs approved, 2 more in pipeline; EDQM audit completed, approval awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Status of Zambia ($25 million) and Europe programmes, and timing of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Zambia POs received after the mid-year election; dispatch Q4 FY27 and revenue in Q1 FY28 after 100-120 days shipping. Europe dossier filed; approval 1-2 quarters away; supplies start FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How will the $100 million European advance be recognised and what is the cash/non-cash split?
qa_highlights.answer: No revenue or P&L impact from the advance in H1 FY27. Revenue recognition starts on dossier and plant approval, with composite accounting spreading the advance over the contract period; detail will be in the notes once approved.

qa_highlights.question: Any BC show-cause notice provisioning (FY19-FY25)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a job-work arrangement; the contract with the marketing company puts NBP-related liability on that company, so no financial liability and no provision.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for the next three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Historical capex about INR300 crores a year, higher this year due to Baddi. Maintenance capex about 5% of INR2,400 crores gross block. No multi-year figures given.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution from Oriflame and when does Baddi contribute?
qa_highlights.answer: Oriflame PAT contribution negligible; revenue to build over a couple of years. Baddi to deliver 10-15% of CDMO revenue in three years.

qa_highlights.question: Why did domestic branded EBITDA fall YoY and what is the PCPM trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Investment in manpower: MRs up from 1,400 to 1,600 plus about 450 line managers. PCPM about 2.5, dragged down by 200 new hires in Q1; mature gynae divisions above 3.2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CDMO growth outlook and how is API pricing moving?
qa_highlights.answer: CDMO growth driven by volume and price; about 60 days of order visibility; volume growth expected to continue. API prices up 2-3% QoQ and 5-7% YoY, with slight upward movement expected in the next 2-3 months.

risks_watch: Zambia revenue recognition slips into Q1 FY28 because of shipping time; the Q4 dispatch must be met.
European dossier approval timing (1-2 quarters) and whether the approval drives a lumpy revenue recognition.

Domestic branded EBITDA recovery depends on PCPM improving from 2.5 as the new field force matures; growth is running at about 8%, below the 8-10% target band (and the double-digit volume guidance cited by an analyst).
Commodity-linked API price volatility; CDMO price realisation depends on API prices, which are rising.
Baddi Phase 1 ramp-up and Oriflame revenue build-up; Oriflame PAT contribution currently negligible.
API still loss-making (INR5-6 crores a quarter); breakeven targeted in 3-4 quarters.
Capex step-up and possible debt funding for Baddi phases; the company has not given a multi-year capex number.
summary.management_tone: Confident on CDMO volumes and the top line, but guarded on timing: management declined to give specific guidance or new contract size, and it deferred Zambia and Europe revenue timing. Answers on API breakeven and trade generics were hedged, with no hard dates given.
key_quotes: The performance was driven by double-digit volume growth during the quarter.
So, the business is, as you rightly said, $25 million fully intact with a margin profile which are slightly better than our CDMO margins.
So no time lines as of now.

adds.what: Baddi Phase 1 oral solids facility, over 6 billion units/year

growth.why: No numeric company-wide revenue guidance; management gives no business-level revenue guidance, but CDMO volume growth above 20% for four quarters and Baddi Phase 1 (6 bn units/yr, 3-4 months out, INR43 cr at Baddi) back a positive outlook, while the Zambia $25m revenue slipped to Q1 FY28 and no Zambia revenue is expected in FY27.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin 14.5% in Q2 FY27 vs 9.3% a year ago and 15% in Q1 FY27, but CDMO EBITDA only +2.9% QoQ and domestic branded PCPM is about 2.5 with the new field force still maturing, so the trend is not clearly up from here.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Baddi Phase 1 (over 6 billion oral solid units/year) is in trial runs and management says it will be operational in 3-4 months and fully operational by Q1 FY28; Oriflame's two acquired plants were integrated in Q2 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: CDMO volume growth has been above 20% YoY and above 20% QoQ for four straight quarters, with about 60 days of order visibility; utilisation is only about 50%, so there is room to absorb it.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is only about 50%, which is well below the 80% threshold, so a new capex round is not forced; but H1 FY27 capex was about INR210 crores, Baddi phases are ongoing and funding via debt is being considered, and no multi-year capex figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no business-level revenue guidance and cut the FY27 Zambia contribution to zero (revenue now booked Q1 FY28); the Europe timeline is 1-2 quarters away and is still unconfirmed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Zambia revenue has already slipped to Q1 FY28 after 100-120 days of transit, and the Europe dossier approval (1-2 quarters) and Baddi ramp could slip; the Q4 FY27 Zambia dispatch must be met.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Akumentis new launches contributed about half of its growth, with about 30 DCGI approvals a year (2-3 per month), and 2 more CEPs are in the pipeline; Oriflame colour cosmetics entry is also underway.

rows.label: Europe contract supply via dossier approval
rows.why: Dossier filed; approval could take 1-2 quarters and supplies start in FY28, with management giving a clearer timeline in about one quarter, so timing is not yet firm.

rows.label: Zambia $25m order (first of two rounds) revenue
rows.why: Purchase orders are in hand and dispatch is due in Q4 FY27; revenue books in Q1 FY28 after 100-120 days of transit, with no Zambia revenue in FY27.

rows.label: API EBITDA breakeven
rows.why: API EBITDA loss narrowed to INR5.7 crores from INR14 crores a year ago on revenue of INR29 crores, and management targets breakeven within 3-4 quarters with no firm date.
